notes: Group chat made to work end to end in a real browser, plus the waveform crash and presentation changes. Two passes, two findings (group events and read receipts reached nobody). Known and not fixed: delete-for-me in a group (needs per-member deletion state), and mod mail's send handler uses the same sender-as-recipient pattern -- both told to the user.

instruments.evidence: c0c83c19b..f96610842: fff569fdf (waveform fits a narrow bubble), e4631903a (groups service routes), c6ba12318 (read receipt in the paged list), 4a100dedf (group readable by members, newest first, new-message broadcast), f96610842 (member count, group sender names, one-button quick reactions). Read 4de5bf23f (mobile list), 464c678c8 and d60e3bee1 (the call and group work), 9cc07e6b7 (G5).

Rendered in the browser pane signed in as DERRF: group rows read 'Test 3 members'; group bubbles name the sender (TestUser, seed_user_1) and own bubbles do not; the quick reactions are one smiley beside the menu, hidden until the message is hovered, the recent emojis opening above it -- and below on the first message, which the list's edge had clipped. A direct message with a voice message opened at 390 px without the error boundary the waveform used to trip.
Printed the real message list for the group through the API: newest first after the fix; the sealed message is group-v1, key version 1, 75 characters of ciphertext.
The ordering change is in SQL: ORDER BY sent_at, id DESC for groups, ASC for mod mail; the cursor comparison follows the order.
groupsService.routes.test.ts reads cmd/server/main.go and requires every call to match a registered method and path.
Group messages carry sender_id; the page maps it through the group's participants (the sidebar's query key).
The participant rule for a group now lives in getConversationParticipantIDs; the new-message broadcast uses it rather than its own copy.
Integration tests create real groups through POST /groups and real sockets through /ws.
Waveform widths 20, 100, 400 and 0.

Siblings of the new-message broadcast, looked for after it was fixed: edits, pins and thread replies go through getConversationParticipantIDs, which treated a group as a direct message and found nobody -- finding group-events-reach-no-member. The read receipt had its own mod-mail-only branch -- finding group-read-receipt-reaches-nobody. Reactions read conversation_participants first and were right.
Broadcast failures are logged; the send still succeeds.
The duplicated member query in broadcastToOtherGroupMembers was folded into the helper.

Every IsParticipant/GetOtherUserID use in the handlers listed. Group-reachable and fixed: MarkAsRead (finding), the participant helper (finding). Group-reachable and not fixed here: DeleteMessage checks message.IsParticipant, which knows only a sender and a recipient -- for a group message both are the sender, so another member cannot hide a message for themselves. That needs per-member deletion state the schema does not have; told to the user. Others (slideshow, folders, conversation archive) are DM features or guarded elsewhere.

Controls: group-events-reach-no-member (helper back to mod mail only: the pin test times out waiting for message_pinned); group-read-receipt-reaches-nobody (branch back to mod mail only: conversation_read never arrives). Both pass at HEAD.

findings.summary: getConversationParticipantIDs read conversation_participants only for mod mail and user1/user2 for everything else, so a group had no participants: edits, pins and thread replies were broadcast to nobody, and encrypted forwarding compared two empty member lists.

control.observed: With the helper back to mod mail only: FAIL, no message_pinned reaches either member within 3 s. At HEAD: PASS.

findings.summary: MarkAsRead sent conversation_read to every participant only for mod mail; a group took the direct-message branch, where GetOtherUserID finds nobody, so no member heard the group had been read.

control.observed: With the branch back to mod mail only: FAIL, conversation_read never reaches the other member. At HEAD: PASS.
